concepts.name: K2 (Godwin-Austen): Status, Location and Administrative Context
key_dimensions: Highest peak in India and second highest in the world — located in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (Gilgit-Baltistan), often a UPSC trap on 'highest peak in Indian territory vs. Indian subcontinent'
Part of the Karakoram Range, not the Greater Himalayas — distinction frequently tested
Alternative names: K2, Mount Godwin-Austen, Chhogori — multiple names create confusion in matching questions
Political sensitivity: Located in PoK, raising questions on de jure vs. de facto Indian territory

concepts.name: Kangchenjunga: Highest Peak in Indian-Administered Territory
key_dimensions: Third highest peak in the world (8,586 m) and the highest peak within Indian-administered territory (Sikkim–Nepal border)
Straddles the border between Sikkim (India) and Nepal — precise boundary location tested in map-based questions
Part of the Greater Himalayan Range; Kangchenjunga National Park and Biosphere Reserve surrounds it — UNESCO World Heritage Site linkage
UPSC trap: Often confused with K2 on 'highest peak in India' — answer depends on whether PoK is considered Indian territory

concepts.name: Nanda Devi: Highest Peak Entirely within Indian Territory
key_dimensions: At 7,816 m, it is the highest peak located entirely within India (Uttarakhand) — critical distinction from Kangchenjunga (border peak)
Part of the Garhwal Himalayas; surrounded by Nanda Devi National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Biosphere Reserve
Inner Sanctuary and Outer Sanctuary — unique concentric protected zone geography tested in environment questions
UPSC trap: Distinguishing 'highest peak in India' vs. 'highest peak entirely within India' — Kangchenjunga vs. Nanda Devi

concepts.name: Karakoram Range: Key Peaks and Geopolitical Significance
key_dimensions: Houses K2, Gasherbrum I & II, Broad Peak, and Masherbrum — all among world's 14 eight-thousanders; concentration tested
Siachen Glacier lies in the Karakoram — strategic military importance and India-Pakistan dispute linkage
Karakoram Pass: historically important trade route on India–China (Xinjiang) border — distinct from Khyber and other passes
Distinction between Karakoram Range and Greater Himalayas — separate orogenic systems, often confused in map questions

concepts.name: Saltoro Ridge and Sia Kangri: Siachen Context Peaks
key_dimensions: Saltoro Ridge is the military control line (AGPL) held by India west of the Siachen Glacier — not the LOC
Sia Kangri (7,422 m) near the junction of India, Pakistan, and China — tri-junction peak geography
These peaks define the strategic high-altitude battlefield; UPSC tests on Saltoro vs. LOC vs. LAC distinctions
Indira Col: northernmost point of Indian territory in this region — named after Indira Gandhi, located at ~5,764 m on the Siachen Glacier

concepts.name: Peaks of Himachal Pradesh: Highest Summits and Their Ranges
key_dimensions: Reo Purgyil (6,816 m): highest peak of Himachal Pradesh, located near Spiti on the India–China border — frequently tested in state-wise highest peak questions
Part of the Zanskar Range — not the main Himalayan range; range identification is a key dimension
Shilla Peak (~6,111 m) in Spiti: formerly claimed as highest in HP, now superseded — historical vs. current data trap
Leo Pargial as alternative spelling — name variation trap in UPSC options

concepts.name: Peaks of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh: Nun-Kun Massif
key_dimensions: Nun (7,135 m) and Kun (7,077 m) form a twin-peak massif in the Zanskar Range — highest peaks in the Zanskar Range
Located in the Kargil district of Ladakh UT — post-2019 reorganization changes administrative location from J&K to Ladakh UT
Distinction: Nun-Kun is in Zanskar Range while K2/Saltoro peaks are in Karakoram — range-peak mapping trap
Nun is the highest peak in Jammu & Kashmir/Ladakh region outside Karakoram — nuanced ranking question

concepts.name: Peaks of the Eastern Himalayas: Arunachal Pradesh
key_dimensions: Kangto (7,090 m) and Nyegi Kangsang (7,047 m) — among the highest peaks in Arunachal Pradesh, part of Assam Himalayas
Gorichen (6,538 m): highest peak of Arunachal Pradesh, part of Kangrigakar Range — tested in state highest peak lists
McMahon Line proximity — peaks near disputed India–China boundary make them geopolitically significant
UPSC trap: Eastern Himalayas peaks are less prominent globally but tested for state-level geography and border context

concepts.name: Peaks of Uttarakhand: Garhwal and Kumaon Himalaya
key_dimensions: Nanda Devi (7,816 m) vs. Kamet (7,756 m) vs. Trisul (7,120 m) — ranking and range identification within Uttarakhand
Kamet: second highest peak in Uttarakhand, located in the Zaskar Range near Mana Pass — range confusion trap
Badrinath Peak, Kedarnath Peak, Gangotri group (Shivling, Bhagirathi peaks) — pilgrim peaks with dual religious-geographic significance
Distinction between peaks in Garhwal Division vs. Kumaon Division — Nanda Devi (Kumaon), Kamet/Badrinath (Garhwal)

concepts.name: Siwaliks and Sub-Himalayan Peaks: Lower Ranges
key_dimensions: Siwaliks (Outer Himalayas) have no significant named peaks above 2,000 m — important negative knowledge for UPSC
Dun valleys (Dehradun, Patlidun) lie between Siwaliks and Lesser Himalayas — geographic context of low-lying zones
Lesser Himalayas peaks: Mussoorie, Shimla, Dharamsala ridges — hill station geography linked to range identification
Pir Panjal Range (sub-range of Lesser Himalayas): highest peak Tatakooti (~4,745 m) — separates Kashmir Valley from Jammu

concepts.name: Peninsular India Peaks: Western Ghats Highest Summits
key_dimensions: Anamudi (2,695 m): highest peak in Peninsular India and South India, located in Kerala (Eravikulam National Park) — Nilgiri Biosphere context
UPSC trap: Anamudi is often listed as highest peak 'south of the Himalayas' which is incorrect — Himalayan peaks are far higher; it is highest in Peninsular India
Doddabetta (2,637 m): highest peak of the Nilgiris; Kudremukh (1,892 m): highest in Karnataka — state-wise ranking tested
Agasthyamalai (1,868 m): southernmost significant peak, straddles Kerala–Tamil Nadu border; Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve linkage

concepts.name: Eastern Ghats Peaks vs. Western Ghats: Comparative Heights
key_dimensions: Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and lower; highest point is Arma Konda (1,680 m) in Andhra Pradesh — lesser known, frequently tested
Jindhagada Peak (~1,690 m) in Andhra Pradesh — rival claim to highest point in Eastern Ghats, data inconsistency trap
Mahendragiri (~1,501 m) in Odisha/AP border — another Eastern Ghats peak with mythological significance tested in cultural geography
Key contrast: Western Ghats rise sharply from Arabian Sea (escarpment), Eastern Ghats are gradual and eroded — structural geomorphology tested alongside peak data

concepts.name: Peaks of Northeast India: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur Plateaus
key_dimensions: Shillong Peak (~1,965 m): highest point of the Shillong Plateau (Meghalaya); a residual plateau, not Himalayan — geomorphic classification trap
Saramati (3,826 m): highest peak in Nagaland and highest in Patkai-Naga range — tested in state-wise highest peak questions
Japfu Peak (3,048 m) in Nagaland: second highest; Blue Naga hills context
Mount Iso (~2,994 m) or Manipur Ukhrul peaks — less known, tested to differentiate Northeast states' highest points

concepts.name: Volcanic Peaks of India: Andaman & Nicobar Context
key_dimensions: Barren Island: only active volcano in South Asia and India, located in Andaman Sea — 'only' clause heavily tested
Narcondam Island: dormant (not extinct) stratovolcano in Andaman & Nicobar — UPSC trap on active vs. dormant vs. extinct classification
Saddle Peak (732 m): highest point of Andaman & Nicobar Islands, located in North Andaman — island peaks often neglected in preparation
Mount Thullier (642 m): highest point of Great Nicobar Island — distinction between Andaman group and Nicobar group peaks

concepts.name: Passes Adjacent to Important Peaks: Peak-Pass Spatial Relationships
key_dimensions: Rohtang Pass (3,978 m) near Rohtang massif, Himachal — connects Kullu Valley to Lahaul-Spiti; Atal Tunnel bypasses it
Zoji La Pass near Greater Himalayas — connects Srinagar to Kargil; proximity to NH-1 (Srinagar-Leh highway) strategic importance
Nathu La (4,310 m) in Sikkim near Kangchenjunga massif — India-China trade route reopened in 2006; historic Silk Route
Shipki La near Reo Purgyil — Sutlej River crosses into China here; river-pass-peak spatial triad frequently tested

concepts.name: Himalayan Glaciers and Their Source Peaks
key_dimensions: Gangotri Glacier originates near Chaukhamba and Gangotri group peaks — source of Bhagirathi (Ganga); glacier retreat data
Zemu Glacier: largest glacier in Eastern Himalayas, originates from Kangchenjunga massif in Sikkim
Siachen Glacier: originates from Sia Kangri/Saltoro Ridge area — world's second longest non-polar glacier; military significance
UPSC trap: Biafo and Baltoro glaciers are in PoK (Karakoram) — not to be confused with Indian-administered glacier systems

concepts.name: State-wise Highest Peaks of India: Comparative Rankings
key_dimensions: Frequently tested combinations: J&K/Ladakh (Nun), HP (Reo Purgyil), Uttarakhand (Nanda Devi), Sikkim (Kangchenjunga), Arunachal (Gorichen) — state-peak matching
Southern states: Kerala (Anamudi), Tamil Nadu (Doddabetta), Karnataka (Mullayanagiri 1,930 m), Andhra Pradesh (Arma Konda)
UPSC trap: Mullayanagiri is often confused — it is the highest peak in Karnataka (Baba Budan Hills, Chikmagalur), not Kudremukh
Island territories: Saddle Peak (A&N), Kardang (Lakshadweep has no significant peaks — coral atolls) — exception tested

concepts.name: Peaks on International Borders: India's Mountain Boundaries
key_dimensions: India–China (LAC) border peaks: Reo Purgyil, Gorichen, Kangto — peaks straddle disputed boundaries making them politically sensitive
India–Nepal border: Kangchenjunga, Api Himal, Saipal — distinction between peaks on border vs. peaks entirely in Nepal (Everest, Annapurna)
India–Pakistan border (LoC/PoK): K2, Gasherbrum, Broad Peak — located in PoK, status in Indian claim vs. ground reality
India–Bhutan border peaks: less prominent, Kangchenjunga massif spills marginally — tri-junction at Bhutan-Sikkim-Tibet

concepts.name: Mountain Ranges and Their Highest Peaks: Range-Peak Mapping
key_dimensions: Karakoram: K2 (8,611 m); Greater Himalayas: Kangchenjunga in India (8,586 m); Zanskar Range: Nun (7,135 m) — range-to-peak mapping
Vindhya Range: Amarkantak (~1,048 m) — highest point and source of Narmada and Son rivers; geomorphic + hydrology trap
Aravalli Range: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) in Rajasthan (Abu Road) — highest peak of Aravallis, oldest fold mountain range in India
Satpura Range: Dhupgarh (1,350 m) near Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh — highest peak of Satpuras; 'Queen of Satpura' = Pachmarhi hill station linkage

concepts.name: Guru Shikhar and Aravalli Peaks: Significance and Traps
key_dimensions: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m): highest point of the Aravalli Range, located in Mount Abu, Rajasthan — only hill station of Rajasthan
Aravallis are the oldest fold mountains in India (Pre-Cambrian) — contrast with younger Himalayas; age-height inverse relationship tested
UPSC trap: Guru Shikhar is sometimes listed as highest peak in Rajasthan — this is correct, but confusion arises with Thar Desert context (no peaks there)
Dilwara Temples at Mount Abu — cultural geography linkage to Guru Shikhar region tested in art & culture questions
